rounds.text: Gujarat Poly Electronics Ltd trades at an extraordinary valuation disconnect, sitting at a P/E of just 1.85x and an EV/EBITDA of 1.7x, which represents a massive discount to sector benchmarks of 21.22x and 11.89x respectively [E1, E6, E11]. The underlying fundamental engine is firing with exceptional momentum, evidenced by a staggering 507% trailing twelve months profit growth and a quarterly operating margin expanding to 15% in September 2026, up six percentage points year-over-year [E18, E27]. Furthermore, the company is effectively debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and generated robust free cash flow of Rs 26 Cr in March 2026 [E32, E33]. This financial strength underpins a discounted cash flow intrinsic value estimate that leaves an enormous 91.8% margin of safety, while a reverse DCF implies the market is irrationally pricing in a catastrophic 30.1% earnings contraction [E39, E40, E41]. Conceded: [E13] the company has posted a negative ROE of -24.9% and long-term sales growth has been sluggish at 4% over five years [E15]. Yet, current operating trends show a clear inflection, with results scoring 100/100 and profit growth outstripping 1-year price performance by 537%, indicating a powerful turnaround that stale sentiment has entirely overlooked [E43, E57].

The company’s fundamental performance is characterized by a negative return on equity of -24.9% [E13, E25] and a weak return on capital employed of only 4.4% [E12]. Reported earnings are heavily reliant on non-operational items, specifically an "other income" of Rs. 30.0 Cr [E49], which explains why operating cash flow remains negative at Rs -1 Cr [E31] and the cash conversion ratio is a dismal -0.04x [E30]. Long-term stagnation is evident in the compounded sales growth of just 2% over the last three years [E16] and 4% over the last decade [E14, E47]. Operational risks are rising as working capital days have surged from -9.63 to 112 days [E50], while operating margins have fallen by 3 percentage points compared to three years ago [E26]. Investors have reacted to these underlying issues with the share price declining 30% over the past year [E22], a sentiment echoed by promoters who reduced their holding by 1.90 percentage points [E36]. Conceded: the company is almost debt-free [E33, E46] and recent quarterly results show an increasing operating-margin trend [E29] and high year-over-year profit growth [E54, E55].

While the bear highlights historical negative returns [E13, E25, E12], current performance indicates a massive turnaround with an ROE of 65.08% and ROCE of 75.46%, which dwarf sector benchmarks of 11.11% and 13.13% respectively [E9, E10]. Although other income impacted reported earnings [E49] and operating cash flow [E31], the business successfully generated Rs 26 Cr in free cash flow [E32]. The stagnation cited by the bear [E14, E16, E47] is refuted by recent 24% YoY sales growth [E52] and a quarterly operating margin that has climbed to 15% [E27], marking an increasing trend over four quarters [E29]. Conceded: working capital days have increased [E50] and the share price has dropped 30% over the last year [E22], but this has resulted in a deep-value P/E of 1.85x [E1] and a 91.8% margin of safety [E40]. With TTM profit growth of 507% [E18] exceeding price growth by 537% [E43], the current market price implies a -30.1% earnings growth that is completely decoupled from the company's accelerating results [E41, E57]. Finally, despite a minor reduction in promoter holding [E36], the company remains almost debt-free [E46] with a P/B of 1.20x [E2], significantly lower than the sector's 2.38x benchmark [E7].

The Bull’s claim of a turnaround based on high ROE and ROCE [E9, E10] is fundamentally undermined by the fact that earnings include a massive Rs 30.0 Cr in other income [E49], while filed statements report a negative ROE of -24.9% [E13] and a meager ROCE of 4.4% [E12]. This reliance on non-operating income explains why the TTM profit growth of 507% [E18] failed to produce operational liquidity, resulting in a negative operating cash flow of Rs -1 Cr [E31] and a poor cash conversion ratio of -0.04x [E30], making the reported free cash flow of Rs 26 Cr [E32] appear disconnected from core business performance. Although quarterly margins have risen [E27], the long-term reality is a stagnant 4% sales growth over ten years [E14] and a dangerous spike in working capital days from -9.63 to 112 days [E50], suggesting the business is struggling to manage its core operations efficiently. The market has recognized these risks, as evidenced by the share price falling 30% over the last year [E22] and 13% over three years [E21], suggesting the low P/E of 1.85x [E1] is a reflection of poor earnings quality rather than a deep-value opportunity. Conceded: the company is almost debt-free [E46] and maintains a low P/B of 1.20x [E2], but the simultaneous reduction in promoter holding [E36] suggests those closest to the business lack confidence in the sustainability of recent results.
